drafts.name: Jeff Pinner

email.subject: Your first months at Exa
email.body:
Hi Jeff,

Congrats on the CTO role. The announcement said Exa has humongous engineering and research to do at larger-than-google-scale, and needs to do it quickly.

My guess is that leaves more infra and product work in the queue than the team can get to. Your team already uses Devin this way: one multi-week session built a test-system contract and rolled it out service by service. At Modal, Devin produces a useful early investigation on 80% of incidents.

Would love 20 minutes to pick one backlog and walk through what scaling that would look like. This week or next?

Best,

drafts.linkedin_note: Hi Jeff, congrats on the CTO role at Exa and on shipping Exa Snapshots as your first launch. I work with teams using Devin to add engineering capacity on infra-heavy roadmaps, and your team already runs it. Would be glad to connect.
drafts.linkedin_followup: Thanks for connecting, Jeff. One thing I left out of my email: your post said Exa will need to operate at scale that is orders of magnitude larger than what humans search on the web today. At that scale the backlog tends to be the unglamorous work around the core, like dependency upgrades, flaky tests and on-call chores. That's the work teams hand to Devin so engineers stay on the hard systems problems. Ramp says Devin fixes tens of thousands of hours of technical debt. Open to comparing notes on where that fits for Exa?

drafts.name: Jeeyoung Kim

email.subject: Robust pipelines, agent-written code
email.body:
Hi Jeeyoung,

I read the Composing a Search Engine post, and the question of how you keep search pipelines robust as most code is written by agents stuck with me.

My guess is review is now where that pressure lands. Devin picks up the ticket, writes the tests and opens a PR, and Devin Review checks agent-written PRs before they merge. Companies' test coverage typically rises from 50-60% to 80-90% with Devin.

Happy to grab 20 minutes and pick one pipeline service to walk through. Does this week or next work?

Best,

drafts.linkedin_note: Hi Jeeyoung, enjoyed the Composing a Search Engine post on keeping search pipelines robust when most code is written by agents. I spend my time with eng leaders working on that review problem. Would be glad to connect.
drafts.linkedin_followup: Thanks for connecting. Separate from the review question: you posted that Exa is especially in need of infra / platform engineers. When hiring lags the roadmap, teams often hand Devin the platform chores that sit in the queue, like dependency upgrades, broken builds and flaky tests, so the engineers you do hire start on the hard problems. Your team already runs Devin across the whole lifecycle, so setup is largely done. Worth comparing notes on which chores would go first?

drafts.name: João Adriano

email.subject: Next wave after the test contract
email.body:
Hi João,

Your line in the Devin story stuck with me: if you feel bottlenecked by how many tasks you can do in parallel end-to-end, you need to go to the cloud. The test-system contract rollout across roughly 30 to 40 PRs is the clearest example of that.

My guess is the next bottleneck is incident load as you provision for Bing-scale traffic. Devin can pick up alerts as they land, investigate, and come back with a PR. At Modal, Devin produces a useful early investigation on 80% of incidents.

Would love 20 minutes to pick the next workstream together. This week or next?

Best,

drafts.linkedin_note: Hi João, loved your take in the Devin story on going to the cloud to parallelize end-to-end work. Also saw you're leading the new Exa Zurich office. Would be glad to connect and hear what's next for infra at Exa.
drafts.linkedin_followup: Thanks for connecting, João. Saw you broke down how your teams evaluate and route models in production at the event GMI Cloud hosted with Notion. Routing changes tend to ripple through evals, configs and tests across many services. Curious whether that kind of change is something you'd hand to Devin next, or whether it stays hands-on for now. Happy to share how other infra teams split that work between people and Devin.
